title: The Silent Hollow Revisited
premise: Dominic Brightwater, a bone-carver who hears the dead, has never left the valley where magic cannot follow — until a child arrives at his door speaking a language older than kingdoms, pursued by riders who serve a court thought extinct. The child carries a carved token Dominic recognizes as his own masterwork, meaning his dead mentor hid a bloodline — and a truth about the valley's silence — inside Dominic's ordinary life. Pursued across a land where his bone-gift grows louder and more dangerous, Dominic must choose between the loyalty his mentor's ghost demands and the truth the child's blood will reveal. In the climax, Dominic speaks the forbidden name of the Hollow's founder before the thirteenth moon turns, shattering the valley's silence and offering the secret to both armies rather than letting either claim it. The war does not reignite; instead the child is adopted by the valley's found family, and Dominic, exiled from his silence, becomes the first voice of a new accord.
about_author: Gideon Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary carvings in remote parish crypts, an experience that seeps into every bone-carved detail of his fiction. He writes fantasy about quiet people dragged into loud histories, and claims he has never once left a draft unfinished — only unburied.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On a frost-bitten night, a mute child arrives clutching a bone token Dominic carved years ago for his dead mentor, speaking a language that makes the valley's dead stir in their graves. When armored riders reach the valley's edge and cannot cross, Dominic realizes the valley's magicless silence is not natural — it was made, and the child is the key. Beat: dread blooming into reluctant protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with interludes of the mentor's ghost. Fleeing through the lowlands, Dominic uses his bone-gift to interrogate the dead about the token, learning his mentor smuggled out the last heir of the Hollow's founder — and that the mentor's ghost has been lying to him for years to keep the valley's secret buried. The riders close in, led by someone who knew Dominic's mentor. Beat: loyalty cracking under the weight of truth.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Dominic and the child, whose language Dominic is finally beginning to understand. Trapped in the ruined Hollow itself as the thirteenth moon wanes, they discover the founder's tomb — and the riders, who are not conquerors but descendants sworn to reclaim the heir and reignite the old war of vengeance. The mentor's ghost begs Dominic to give up the child; the child, in broken words, asks only to be believed. Beat: betrayal, choice, and the gathering storm of the climax.

chapters.title: The First Voice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the tomb's threshold, with both armies assembled beneath the full thirteenth moon, Dominic speaks the founder's true name aloud — a secret meant to start a war — and instead tells the whole truth of the valley's silence: it was built on a massacre both sides committed. The dead themselves testify through him, and the armies' fury collapses into grief. The riders' captain kneels to the child, not as an heir but as a child. Beat: catharsis, and a found family formed in the ruins.
